history.period: 11th century CE (main structure); references to the shrine go back to the 7th century
history.summary: The largest and most prominent temple of Bhubaneswar, dedicated to Shiva as Lingaraja ("King of Lingas"), worshipped as Harihara — a syncretic Shiva-Vishnu form reflecting Odisha's combined Shaiva-Vaishnava tradition. The existing Kalinga-style structure was built in the 11th century by the Somavamshi king Jajati Keshari, with later additions by the Eastern Gangas; the region, Ekamra Kshetra, is celebrated in the Ekamra Purana (13th c.). The central 55 m vimana is the tallest structure in Bhubaneswar. Unlike most old temples here, it is fully active in worship; non-Hindus are not admitted inside the sanctum.

name: Lingaraj Temple
town_description: Bhubaneswar, the capital of Odisha, is known as the "Temple City of India" for its hundreds of ancient temples from the 7th to 13th centuries, the greatest concentration of Kalinga-style architecture anywhere. Once called Ekamra Kshetra (the mango-forest shrine), it sits on the coastal plain between the Mahanadi delta and the Eastern Ghats. Modern Bhubaneswar is a planned administrative and IT hub built around its ancient old town, home to Lingaraj, Puri's Jagannath pilgrims' transit stop, and Biju Patnaik International Airport.
